subject: Entitlement modeling and response-time ladder for on-prem deployment
messages:
From: Judy Park <judy@clinicalai.com>
To: irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Entitlement model & SLAs for on-prem deployment

Hi Irene / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team liked the inference latency and the model catalog approach. We're starting to map commercial options internally and need clarity on two things before procurement can draft an initial RFP:

1) Entitlement/licensing model — do you price by concurrent nodes, total seats, or a hybrid (nodes + per-token overage)? For on-prem we need to show TCO to our finance team.

2) Response-time ladder and escalation — we operate a 24/7 service; procurement wants to know what response and remediation SLAs look like across different support tiers (business-hours, 24x5, 24x7).

Can you share a simple matrix showing three packaging options (pilot, standard deployment, enterprise) including platform fee, typical onboarding retainer, and support response times? If you can attach an example SOW or entitlement matrix that would help speed review.

Also, would Redwood consider amortizing the platform fee over the first 12 months for a pilot? That would make a 6-month technical pilot easier to justify.

Best,
Judy
Judy Park
Head of Procurement, ClinicalAI

From: irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>
To: Judy Park <judy@clinicalai.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-24T11:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Entitlement model & SLAs for on-prem deployment

Judy — thanks for the clear ask. I've attached a compact entitlement matrix and an example SOW to this thread. High level options below — happy to convert into a one-page comparison table for procurement.

Pilot (6 months)
- Licensing: metered on-prem license (per-token) or single reserved dev node at reduced rate.
- Platform fee: waived for first 3 months, then 50% creditable against first-year platform fee.
- Onboarding retainer: one-off (recommended small to cover initial integration).
- Support: business-hours (M-F) with 24-hour response for sev1; optional paid upgrade to 24x5.

Standard Deployment
- Licensing: reserved nodes (node-based) with token overage.
- Platform fee: annual platform fee covering control plane + telemetry.
- Onboarding retainer: typically amortized across year one.
- Support: 24x5 with 4-hour response for sev1; standard CB (cost baseline).

Enterprise
- Licensing: dedicated pool, optional on-prem appliance license with enterprise discounts.
- Platform fee: full annual; discounts available with multi-year commit.
- Onboarding retainer: larger, usually billed upfront; can be offset via credits tied to commit.
- Support: 24x7 with 1-hour response for sev1, named escalation contacts, periodic runbooks.

Attachments: entitlement_matrix_v1.xlsx (xlsx), SOW_sample.pdf (pdf)

Notes for internal team (Marissa / Sean):
- I'm inclined to propose an amortized platform-fee credit for a 6-month pilot (Judy asked explicitly).
- We should present a clear escalation path in the SOW (named contacts + timeline) to satisfy ClinicalAI's ops team.

Marissa — any commercial levers you'd suggest to make pilot acceptance easier while protecting revenue?

Thanks,
Irene Choi
Head of Enterprise Sales, Redwood Inference
[attachment: entitlement_matrix_v1.xlsx (xlsx)]

From: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>, sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-24T13:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Entitlement model & SLAs for on-prem deployment

Quick commercial thoughts — copying Sean for ops / escalation input.

1) Pilot economics
- Offer: waive platform fee for first 3 months, then apply a 50% credit that customers can elect to use against year-1 invoicing if they convert to a paid contract.
- Require minimal commit: either a nominal prepaid onboarding retainer or a one-node reserved dev seat to lock cadence.

2) Discounting and packaging
- Propose a tiered discount schedule tied to committed annual spend (e.g., 5% @ $250k, 10% @ $500k, locked for the first year).
- Avoid deeply discounting the platform fee — instead, structure it as creditable/conditional (reduces churn risk).

3) Support / escalation
- For enterprise: include named on-call rotation, quarterly runbook review, and 1 hour sev1 SLA. For standard: 4 hour sev1 during business hours, 24x5.
- Sean: please confirm our ability to guarantee 1 hour response for sev1 on dedicated pools and any restrictions.

I'll draft a commercial bullet list for Procurement that keeps us flexible but gives them the pilot they want.

Marissa Cole
Director, Enterprise Sales — Redwood Inference
[internal note: favor crediting, not discounting platform fee; protects ARR and keeps path to expansion]

From: Judy Park <judy@clinicalai.com>
To: irene_choi <irene@redwood.com>
Cc: marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-05-25T08:47:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Entitlement model & SLAs for on-prem deployment

Thanks — this is exactly what procurement needed to see. A couple quick clarifications before we route to legal/finance: 

- Can you give a concrete example invoice for year one under the pilot-convert flow (node pricing + platform fee credit applied)? A sample numbers worksheet would be ideal.
- Will Redwood commit in the SOW to the named escalation contacts and the 1 hour sev1 response for Enterprise? We need that in writing for our SOC review.
- For the pilot: ClinicalAI is comfortable with a small prepaid onboarding retainer if the platform fee credit is applied on conversion.

If possible, can you also confirm whether the platform fee can be capitalized for our finance team (they asked about CAPEX treatment of platform fee vs ops expense).

I'll send along our security questionnaire separately (attached) — legal wants to cross-check the SOW runbook and incident handling.

Best,
Judy Park
Head of Procurement, ClinicalAI
